points.description: States that the statement is FALSE.
Justification: the interrupted process is NOT always rescheduled immediately after the interrupt handler completes; the control need not return to the paused process.
Justification: another process can be scheduled (dispatched by the scheduler) on the CPU next.
Gives the specific reason: the time slice (quantum) of the first process expires, so the scheduler picks a different process.
points.partial_credit: Only mentions pre-emption/scheduler picking another process without naming time slice expiry: no part marks.

rubric.notes: Full marks need FALSE plus a justification that another process can run next because the interrupted process's time slice expired. A TRUE answer, or no correct justification, gets 0 overall. Vague statements such as "scheduler decides" without the time slice reason lose P4; a wrong claim in the justification loses the affected point.
